title: Liverpool have suffered from VAR decisions going against them the ‘whole season’, Arne Slot says
content:
Arne Slot believes Liverpool have suffered from a succession of contentious video assistant referee decisions this season — but admits they only had themselves to blame for Sunday’s 3-2 defeat to Manchester United.

The Dutch head coach was unhappy that Benjamin Sesko’s goal was allowed to stand at Old Trafford when replays appeared to show the ball hit the striker’s fingers before it bobbled over the line. It put United 2-0 up inside 14 minutes after Matheus Cunha had opened the scoring.

“If a ball has a certain curve and the curve changes, there must have been contact,” Slot told reporters post-match. “The rule is if there was a touch then it should have been disallowed.

“I don’t think it’s a surprise to anyone this season that if there’s a VAR intervention or if there’s something that could be left or right (50-50) then the decision goes against us. That has been the whole season, every single time the same.

“I remember Paris Saint-Germain at home (in the quarter-final of the Champions League), getting a penalty for a soft touch on (Alexis) Mac Allister but of course the VAR intervenes and says: ‘No, no, no, this is not a penalty.’ Then when I see PSG play against Bayern Munich after that same sort of soft touch the penalty stays.

“I saw last week my goalkeeper on the floor with an injury and the referee didn’t stop the game. I see a player of United off the pitch today and the referee stops the game when we try to play on.

“But the second goal we didn’t concede because of a handball, we conceded it because we lost the ball in a stupid position and we lost a few big moments afterwards in duels. We have to first look at ourselves, but that decisions have gone every single game against us, that’s also completely clear and obvious.”

A depleted Liverpool side launched a spirited second-half fightback through goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Cody Gakpo but paid the price for more poor defending when Kobbie Mainoo fired home the winner.

It leaves Slot’s side still needing four points from their remaining three games to guarantee Champions League qualification. Liverpool were also without Alexander Isak, who the head coach said had a “really small injury”.

“I haven’t spoken about all our missing players and I’m not talking about it now,” Slot added. “If you can play a second half like we did, there is no necessity to have other players here. We were able with this team to have a chance of winning this game and we were quite close.

“But as always one moment of switching off immediately leads to us conceding a goal. So many times this season it was waiting for us to score one and then we concede because we switch off for a few seconds in a crucial moment.”
